concepts.label: Analytics Query API (Cluster.analyticsQuery / AnalyticsOptions / AnalyticsResult)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the SDK-side call surface for issuing queries to the Analytics Service (CBAS) from the Java SDK; distinct from the already-promoted server-side analytics:* vocabulary, which describes the service/data model itself rather than how a client talks to it

relations.subject: sdk:analytics-query
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a component's dependency on a named Couchbase service
relations.evidence: This page covers using our operational Java SDK to connect to the Analytics Service of a Capella Operational or self-managed Couchbase Server cluster.

relations.subject: sdk:analytics-query
relations.evidence: This is the analytic counterpart to our [operational data focussed Query Service](sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md).

relations.subject: sdk:analytics-query
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate for a capability depending on a shared underlying mechanism, rather than dependsOnService (a service-to-service dependency, used above for a different fact on this page)
relations.evidence: In addition to the blocking API on `Cluster`, the SDK provides reactive and async APIs on `ReactiveCluster` or `AsyncCluster` respectively.

notable_absence.finding: The page shows AnalyticsResult.metaData().metrics().executionTime() as an in-application way to read query timing, but never states whether Analytics queries are also captured by the SDK's own ThresholdLoggingTracer/LoggingMeter observability surfaces documented elsewhere in this batch - those pages' sample JSON blobs break results out by service name ('kv', 'query'), but this page gives no equivalent 'cbas'/'analytics' example, so the connection is left unasserted rather than assumed.

cross_product_finding: The page's own tip block draws a product-line distinction not otherwise foregrounded in the SDK docs: 'SDKs for Enterprise Analytics ... are available for the .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, and Python platforms' are ordinary operational SDKs, while 'Capella Analytics SDKs (also known as Columnar SDKs)' are a separate SDK family, because Capella Analytics 'does not have Enterprise Analytics' load balancer, and uses a different connection protocol.' This page's own cluster.analyticsQuery() API is neither of those - it talks only to self-managed/Capella-Operational CBAS - so 'the Java SDK' covers at least three distinct client libraries across the word 'Analytics'.
